# RevoTask: Design

Architecture, data model (including the `Card` model with `db.Column(db.Float)`), and a table per slice mapping each requirement to a Flask route or Next.js page, its handler, service, schema and authorization.

## Contents

- 00 Foundation
- 01 Auth Users

## 00 Foundation

### Architecture

A modular-monolith Flask API (`backend/app/blueprints/<feature>/{routes,service,schema}.py`) and a Next.js App Router frontend (`frontend/src`). The browser calls the API directly with a bearer token; Server Components call it with the token read from a cookie.

```
Browser ──(Bearer JWT)──▶ Flask API ──▶ PostgreSQL
   ▲                          ▲
   └── Next.js (Vercel) ──────┘   Server Components use API_BASE_URL and the session cookie
```

Request path in the API: `route` (auth + validate) → `service` (authorization + business rules + transaction) → `models`. Errors are raised as typed `ApiError`s and rendered by one central handler.

### Data model

Eight tables, all with a UUID primary key (`db.Uuid`) and UTC timestamps (DB-01, DB-02). Content tables are soft-deleted (DB-03).

| Table           | Columns (besides `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`)                                                                   |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `users`         | `name`, `email` (unique, lower-case), `password_hash`                                                                |
| `boards`        | `name`, `owner_id` → users, `deleted_at`                                                                             |
| `board_members` | `board_id`, `user_id`, `role` (`admin`/`member`); unique `(board_id, user_id)`                                       |
| `columns`       | `board_id`, `name`, `order` (Float), `is_done`, `deleted_at`                                                         |
| `cards`         | `column_id`, `title`, `description`, `order` (Float), `assignee_id`, `created_by`, `column_entered_at`, `deleted_at` |
| `comments`      | `card_id`, `user_id`, `content`, `deleted_at`                                                                        |
| `notifications` | `user_id`, `type`, `message`, `card_id`, `board_id`, `read_at`                                                       |

The `Card` model (`backend/app/models/card.py`):

```python
class Card(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = "cards"
    id = db.Column(db.Uuid, primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
    column_id = db.Column(db.Uuid, db.ForeignKey("columns.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), nullable=False, index=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    order = db.Column(db.Float, nullable=False)  # FLOAT ordering strategy (DB-04)
    assignee_id = db.Column(db.Uuid, db.ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True, index=True)
    created_by = db.Column(db.Uuid, db.ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True)
    column_entered_at = db.Column(db.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False, default=utcnow)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False, default=utcnow)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False, default=utcnow, onupdate=utcnow)
    deleted_at = db.Column(db.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)
```

### Decisions

- **Envelope.** `{"data": ...}` or `{"error": "<string>", "code": ..., "details": ...}` (`docs/contracts/error-contract.md`). The scaffold's object-shaped `error` was replaced to match the assignment (CHANGELOG R01).
- **Configuration.** One `build_config()`; no literal secrets; production fails fast (CHANGELOG R02).
- **Session.** JWT kept in `AuthContext` and mirrored in a `SameSite=Lax` cookie so Server Components can fetch. Trade-off recorded in `docs/adr/0003-session-storage.md`.
- **Server vs client.** Pages are Server Components that fetch; `BoardView`, forms, hooks and modals are client leaves (FE-04).
- **Completion.** "Completed this week" means a live card whose `column_entered_at` is in the current ISO week and whose column has `is_done = true`. No separate status field is stored.
- **Migrations.** `0001_initial_schema` was reviewed by hand; two defects in the autogenerated output were fixed (CHANGELOG R08).

### Data

`users(id, name, email unique lower-case, password_hash, created_at, updated_at)`. Registration also inserts one `welcome` notification in the same transaction (see 05-notifications).

### Behaviour notes

- **Hashing.** `werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash(method="scrypt")`; tests use `pbkdf2:sha256:1000` via the `PASSWORD_HASH_METHOD` config for speed only.
- **Constant-ish login time.** When the email is unknown, `check_password_hash` runs against a module-level dummy hash.
- **Token.** `create_access_token(identity=str(user.id))`; lifetime from `JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES`. All JWT failures use the envelope with `401` (library default `422` is overridden).
- **Session on the web.** `AuthProvider` receives the cookie token from the root layout, validates it with `GET /users/me`, schedules a sign-out at `exp`, and exposes `api`, `login`, `logout`, `setUser`. See ADR 0003 for why the cookie is readable by JavaScript.
- **Open redirect.** `safeNext()` accepts only values starting with a single `/`.
- **Email enumeration trade-off.** Registration returns `409` for an existing email because the UX benefit outweighs the leak for this product; login stays generic.

| REQ-BOARD-6 | `GET/POST /api/boards/<id>/members`, `PATCH/DELETE /api/boards/<id>/members/<user_id>` | `boards/routes.py`                                                                | `service.list_members`, `add_member`, `set_member_role`, `remove_member` | `MemberAddSchema`, `MemberUpdateSchema`, `MemberSchema` | `require_member` (list), `require_admin` (change) |

### Model

`boards(id, name, owner_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at)` and `board_members(id, board_id, user_id, role, created_at, updated_at)` with `UNIQUE(board_id, user_id)` and `CHECK (role in ('admin','member'))`.

### Behaviour notes

- `require_member` and `require_admin` in `boards/service.py` are the single authorization entry points reused by columns, cards, comments and analytics (BE-08).
- The board detail runs three queries: members, columns, and one `IN` query for cards; cards are grouped to columns in memory (DB-09).
- Soft-delete cascade updates comments, cards, then columns, because each statement selects through its still-live parent; all rows share one timestamp.
- The last-admin rule counts admins in the same transaction before changing a role or removing a member.

### Models

`Column` and `Card` as in 00-foundation. Both have `order = db.Column(db.Float, nullable=False)`; reads use `ORDER BY order, created_at, id`. `cards` has a composite index on `(column_id, order)`.

### Ordering

Server and client share the rules in `docs/contracts/ordering.md`: append `+1024`, prepend `first/2`, insert at the midpoint. `needs_rebalance()` in `columns/service.py` checks adjacent gaps against `MIN_GAP = 1e-6`.

### Drag and drop sequence

1. `dragstart` records the card id.
2. `drop` on a column reads each card's bounding rectangle and counts cards above the pointer (`dropIndexFromPointer`) to get the target index.
3. `orderForIndex` turns the index into a float from the neighbours (ignoring the dragged card).
4. `applyMove` updates state at once; the original card is kept for rollback.
5. `PATCH /position` runs. On success the server's card replaces the local one and `rebalanced` triggers `router.refresh()`. On failure `placeCard(original)` restores it and `useErrorHandler` toasts.

### Notes

- `PATCH /api/cards/<id>` deliberately does not accept `order` or `column_id`; moves go only through `/position` so `CardPositionSchema` is the single gate.
- Cards can only move within their board (`INVALID_MOVE`).
- Listing endpoints exclude deleted columns, cards and boards, and join `board_members` so a user never sees cards of boards they left.

## 04 Comments Activity

### Routes and pages

| REQ       | Interface                       | Handler                                                                       | Service                            | Schema               | Authorization                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| REQ-CMT-1 | `POST /api/cards/<id>/comments` | `comments/routes.py::add_comment`                                             | `comments/service.py::add_comment` | `CommentWriteSchema` | `require_card_member`                   |
| REQ-CMT-2 | `GET /api/cards/<id>/comments`  | `comments/routes.py::list_comments`                                           | `service.list_comments`            | `CommentSchema`      | `require_card_member`                   |
| REQ-CMT-3 | `PATCH /api/comments/<id>`      | `comments/routes.py::edit_comment`                                            | `service.edit_comment`             | `CommentWriteSchema` | membership + `comment.user_id == actor` |
| REQ-CMT-4 | `DELETE /api/comments/<id>`     | `comments/routes.py::delete_comment`                                          | `service.delete_comment`           | n/a                  | membership + owner                      |
| REQ-CMT-5 | card dialog                     | `components/board/CardDetailModal.tsx`, `components/comments/CommentList.tsx` | `lib/api.ts::comments`             | n/a                  | owner-only buttons (UI hint only)       |

### Model

`comments(id, card_id, user_id, content, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at)`; `user_id` is `RESTRICT` so deleting a user can never silently erase content (DB-05). `Comment.author` is a joined relationship so a list is one query.

### Behaviour notes

- `_require_owner` first checks that the caller is still a board member (a removed member cannot edit), then that they wrote the comment. Both failures are `403`.
- `CommentWriteSchema` has no `user_id` field and rejects unknown keys, so the author can only come from the token (BE-07).
- A new comment notifies the card's assignee and creator, excluding the author (see 05-notifications).
- The UI hides Edit and Delete for others' comments as a convenience; the API enforces ownership regardless.

## 05 Notifications

### Routes and pages

| REQ         | Interface                                | Handler                                                                           | Service                                                  | Schema                                  | Authorization                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| REQ-NOTIF-1 | `GET /api/notifications?page=&per_page=` | `notifications/routes.py::list_notifications`                                     | `notifications/service.py::list_notifications`           | `PageQuerySchema`, `NotificationSchema` | `@jwt_required`, filtered by `user_id` |
| REQ-NOTIF-2 | `PATCH /api/notifications/<id>/read`     | `notifications/routes.py::mark_read`                                              | `service.mark_read`                                      | `NotificationSchema`                    | owner or `404`                         |
| REQ-NOTIF-3 | header bell                              | `components/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx`                                   | `hooks/useNotifications.ts`, `lib/api.ts::notifications` | n/a                                     | signed in                              |
| REQ-NOTIF-4 | domain events                            | `auth/service.py`, `cards/service.py`, `comments/service.py`, `boards/service.py` | `notifications/service.py::notify`                       | n/a                                     | n/a                                    |

### Model

`notifications(id, user_id, type, message, card_id, board_id, read_at, created_at, updated_at)` with an index on `(user_id, created_at)`. The API exposes `read` (boolean) derived from `read_at`.

### Behaviour notes

- `notify()` only stages a row; the calling service commits, so a notification exists if and only if the action that caused it committed.
- `unread_count` is computed in one aggregate query, independent of the page requested.
- Polling uses a 30 s `setInterval` with an in-flight guard rather than recursive timeouts, so a slow response never causes overlapping requests.
- The bell is a `BaseButton`; its panel is a labelled region closed by Escape or an outside click.

## 06 Analytics Dashboard

### Routes and pages

| REQ                | Interface                        | Handler                                                             | Service                                 | Schema            | Authorization               |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------- |
| REQ-ANL-1, REQ-ANL-2, REQ-ANL-3, REQ-ANL-4 | `GET /api/boards/<id>/analytics` | `analytics/routes.py::board_analytics`                              | `analytics/service.py::board_analytics` | `AnalyticsSchema` | `require_admin`             |
| REQ-ANL-5          | board header action              | `components/board/AnalyticsModal.tsx` (opened from `BoardView.tsx`) | `lib/api.ts::boards.analytics`          | n/a               | admin-only button (UI hint) |

### Queries (all SQLAlchemy joins in `analytics/service.py`)

- **Cards per column:** `Column LEFT OUTER JOIN Card ON card.column_id = column.id AND card.deleted_at IS NULL`, `GROUP BY` column, ordered by `order`. The outer join keeps empty columns.
- **Completed this week:** `Card JOIN Column` filtered by `Column.is_done` and `Card.column_entered_at >= week_start`.
- **Member activity:** `User JOIN BoardMember` for the roster, plus three grouped queries (`Card JOIN Column` by assignee, the same restricted to done columns this week, `Comment JOIN Card JOIN Column` by author) merged by user id. Separate queries avoid the row multiplication that chaining several outer joins would cause.

### Behaviour notes

- `week_start(now)` is Monday 00:00 UTC of the ISO week; the service accepts an injectable `now` so the boundary is testable.
- Completion is derived from `is_done` plus `column_entered_at`, so toggling a column's `is_done` flag corrects the numbers retroactively and no status column needs maintaining.
- Total cost is five queries regardless of board size.
